entries.statement: Ownership guard: a chain walk never crosses into an AniList entry already claimed by another canonical series (series.anilist_id or series_components.anilist_id), so deliberate splits are safe by construction whatever a source's continuous numbering suggests.

entries.notes: Callers pass excludeSeriesId to re-walk their own series. Consumers: stitch, afg-expansion, afg-extend, canon-tier, reconcile-structure.

entries.statement: Forward chain walk stops the moment the target episode numbering is covered, so a sequel that is a SEPARATE series by ruling is never swallowed; a SEQUEL edge to a MOVIE/OVA/SPECIAL (bridge format) is followed only when the TV path dead-ends before the target is covered; more than one candidate sequel or prequel is an ambiguity and the walk refuses; at most 15 hops.

where.loc: line 16-25 formats + MAX_CHAIN; line 81-113 walkForward; line 115-134 walkChain prequel walk

bundle_parts: bridge formats only when no TV sequel

entries.statement: Prequel side-story fallback: if walking back to the head lands the chain's episode sum more than 2 away from the target (or ambiguous), retry forward-only from the matched entry itself and keep whichever chain fits the numbering better.
witnesses: One Piece (MONSTERS ONA marked as prequel)
entries.notes: Replaced the old berserk-2016 override.

entries.statement: Chain aggregate: id = slugify(head title); title/cover/format/season/tags/synopsis from the head; synonyms/genres/studios/external_links deduped across the chain; end_date from the tail only when finished; total_episodes null unless every component's total is known; aired = sum; popularity/favourites/trending = max; average_score = popularity-weighted mean; is_adult if any; manga picked from the head unless head.source is ORIGINAL.
entries.notes: DRIFT vs resolve.ts: inline source_type lacks DOUJINSHI/ONE_SHOT and the no-source-but-manga-edge fallback; inline manga_status map lacks CANCELLED→finished; id assignment lacks the prior-id lookup/tiebreakers; applyScope is NOT applied inside aggregate (callers apply it).

entries.statement: Component spans: a component with nothing aired holds NO span (episode_start/end null — a 0-length entry would produce start > end); episode_end is set only when the total is known or the component is airing; kind derives from format (MOVIE→movie, OVA→ova, SPECIAL→special, else season); in-flow extras (Kizumonogatari pattern) are written with null ranges after the component they follow.
entries.notes: Replaces ALL components for the series (delete then insert).

entries.statement: AFG never influences episode TYPES where AFL exists — AFL is the type authority; AFG's red/blue/unstyled cell classes (filler/mixed/canon) are used only for expansion series where AFL is absent.
entries.notes: comment-only in lib (the precedence is enforced by callers afg-expansion/afg-extend, not here). CONTRADICTED by resolve.ts line 191-192 'AFL/AFG advisory only' (Sean 2026-08-25) and by the many overrides where AFL 'dissents'. Also: eyeshield-21 import took AFG titles but never mapped its filler flag — the AFG type field went unused there.

entries.statement: AFG chapters-cell parse: ', ' or ';' separate entries while bare commas are thousands separators ('1,144'); ranges 'a-b' / 'a–b' / 'a to b' expand only when b ≥ a and the span is under 500; decimals are kept (bonus chapters); values ≤ 0 or ≥ 10000 are parse artifacts and dropped.
entries.notes: 'no manga has 10k chapters'.

entries.statement: AFG page parse guards: single-cell divider lines ('<—— Pelicula 2 ——>') never become the running arc label; header rows skipped; the episode cell must be strictly 'N.' (1-4 digits) so summary/colspan rows never digit-concatenate into fake numbers; placeholder title cells like '(01).' normalize to an empty (pending) title; AFG's '* Filler' marker inside the title cell is stripped (it is annotation, not the name); type comes from the number cell's class (red=filler, blue=mixed, else canon); an episode repeated across tables keeps its first occurrence.
bundle_parts: divider rows are not arc labels (Naruto 6-27 regression)
strip trailing '* Filler' from title (Sean's eyeshield report)
entries.notes: Watch-order surfacing is the fractional pipeline's job, not the arc field's.

entries.statement: Canonical adaptation-list serialization: chapters_adapted is comma-separated, consecutive integer runs compressed to ranges, ORDER PRESERVED AS ADAPTED (never sorted), fractional values kept inline.
entries.notes: c3.ts parses this format back (strips parentheticals, extracts integers).

entries.statement: Derived AFG anchor per row: the position (end) chapter is the highest MAINLINE (integer) chapter, the start is the first mainline chapter (real source data — display anchors at starts), fractional values are bonus entries and never drive position, and a bonus-only row yields no anchor (research's call).
entries.notes: start_chapter captured at the writer rather than re-derived by formula downstream.

entries.statement: Anchor monotonicity / spike filter: chapters never decrease as episodes advance, so derived anchors keep only the longest non-decreasing chapter subsequence — stray values (divider digits merged into a row, flash-forward grafts) are outliers against the chart's own trend and drop, without the old arc-pattern guard that nuked whole stretches.
entries.notes: Supersedes the arc-pattern guard (Naruto 6-27 regression).

entries.statement: Start sanity (Oshi ep-4): a derived row's start is recomputed as the lowest mainline chapter that is ≥ the previous kept row's end and ≤ its own end (a split chapter is shared — equal is legal; a start one BELOW the previous end is chart double-listing noise, not data); off-trend values stay recorded in chapters_adapted; research-tier starts are exempt.
witnesses: Oshi no Ko (ep 4 listed a stray 10 beside 17-19)
entries.notes: The audit class name anchor_start_offtrend is cited by CONTINUA_SUPPRESSED (resolve.ts line 118), not here; linking it is an inference for the merge to confirm.

entries.statement: Continua parse: the heading is captured (never trusted blindly); frontier episode taken from 'ended at episode N' (absolute) or from 'last canon episode … is Nth of Season S' only when S is 1 or absent (season-relative numbers are not absolute); frontier chapter = max of the 'corresponds to Chapters …' list; continue chapter from 'start reading from Chapter N'; volume + collected range from 'Volume V (collects chapters a to b)'.
entries.notes: Comment: 'Wikipedia + research stay co-verifiers everywhere (Sean: AFG coverage never limits the other sources)' — comment-only principle.

entries.statement: AFL page integrity: the page states its data twice (episode table and Quick List, both semantically classed); per type the table's episode set must equal the Quick List's, and mismatches are reported so the caller refuses the page (parse_integrity).
entries.notes: lib computes integrity.ok; the refusal itself lives in callers (stageAfl does NOT check page.integrity — verify in the scripts/edge homes where it is checked).

entries.statement: AFL row parse: episode 0 is real (OVAs/prologues) and only negative numbers are rejected; duplicate rows with the same number AND type collapse to one, while same-number rows with differing types are kept so the integrity check flags the page instead of silently picking a side; canonicalSlug is read from the first episode link for the alias-corruption check.
Wikipedia volume boundaries: volume N spans [its first chapter start .. next volume's first start − 1]; the final volume stays open (null end).

Monotonic-start gate: chapter starts must strictly increase with volume number; a volume whose start is ≤ the previous kept start is a parse artifact, is DROPPED, and the remaining rows re-close around the gap (a slightly coarser self-consistent table beats a precise-looking contradictory one — the Ippo v61 partial-boundary principle); dropped rows are returned so callers can flag the manga for research.
witnesses: Sailor Moon (v3 'chs 10-3'; 24 rows across 11 manga were live)
entries.notes: Consumers: volumes-backfill, heal-volume-boundaries, audit-ui-truth; toBoundaries (drop-blind) used only by parser-check.

entries.statement: Wikipedia fractional episode numbers (35.5, 13.5, 0.5) are the community convention for specials/OVAs/movies slotted BETWEEN episodes without being counted — exactly our order-only concept; their presence proves the page shares our numbering space; they may describe order-only components but are never episode rows.
entries.notes: comment-only in lib: parseEpisodeList returns fractional numbers unchanged; the caller (wiki-episodes-backfill) must exclude them. Related: mashle 6.5 fractional ruling 2026-08-25.

entries.statement: Wikipedia page discovery: prefix-search 'List of X chapters|episodes' families first; the full-text fallback accepts a hit only when its inner title shares ≥ 50% tokens with a candidate title — search ranking alone is not identity.
witnesses: My Dress-Up Darling (search once returned 'List of Ranma ½ chapters')
entries.notes: findEpisodePages duplicates findChapterPages verbatim (two copies of the same token-agreement logic; a third copy is resolve.ts#titlesAgree with stop-words).

entries.statement: Wikipedia episode-list parse: the overall EpisodeNumber is preferred; a lone EpisodeNumber on a season page may be season-relative and the CALLER's alignment gate decides trustworthiness; rows dedupe by number (first occurrence wins); transclusion targets ({{:Page}}) are extracted for depth-1 follow because main lists often hold only season markers.
witnesses: dr-stone (list holds only {{:Dr. Stone season N}} markers)
entries.notes: Episode-data initiative §12.19d. The alignment gate is NOT in lib.

entries.statement: AFL slug → AniList id matching runs in confidence order — source_map (including manual overrides, method 'manual') → AniFiller seed (confidence 1.0, verified) → exact title match (0.95) → synonym match (0.85) — and anything ambiguous files a match_ambiguous flag and matches NOTHING; guessing is what the flag queue exists to prevent.
bundle_parts: AniFiller seed = fact only, never its episode data (unlicensed)
exact title over romaji/english/native, series formats (TV/TV_SHORT/ONA) outrank on ties
entries.notes: Consumers are all history/one-shot scripts (pilot, backfill, refix, fix-mismatch, wayback-recover2) — no cron uses matchSlug. Witness in text: 'Monster' the TV series must outrank 'Monster' the music video.

entries.statement: One AniList id per AFL slug: if persisting a match hits the unique constraint because another AFL slug already owns the AniList id, the match is refused and a match_ambiguous flag names the owner — two AFL pages for one series needs a merge ruling.
entries.notes: Postgres 23505.

entries.statement: C3 skip-note predicate: a continue point sitting STRICTLY below chapters the same episode already covered must carry a note telling the reader which chapters to skip on arrival; continue == an adapted chapter is C1 (mid-chapter straddle, re-reading intended, never 'skip'); parenthesized page/graft facts in chapters_adapted are stripped before number extraction so page spans never masquerade as chapters; fractional chapters are ignored.
bundle_parts: ahead = integer chapters in chapters_adapted strictly > continue_chapter
note stamp format 'C3 (Sean 2026-08-25): … skip on arrival unless re-reading.' capped at 600 chars
entries.notes: THE single definition, consumed by the parity healer (research/batch15/apply-parity-continues.ts stamps notes) and audit-ui-truth's continue_skip_unnoted class. Note the healer lives under research/batch15/, not scripts/ingest/ proper. 'both' here = writer (healer) + audit, not display.

entries.statement: MangaUpdates identity is NEVER title-guessed: the MangaDex bridge verifies it (a MangaDex entry carrying links.al == our AniList manga id AND links.mu; the mu slug base36-decodes to the numeric id, legacy numeric ids verbatim); no verified bridge → no MU data (flag, don't guess).
entries.notes: The flag-on-no-bridge is the caller's (mu-backfill); lib just returns null.

entries.statement: MU change detection hashes only the fields our rules act on (latest_chapter, status, completed, type, anime) — rating/rank churn must not fake a change every fetch; the FULL MU payload is still staged (greedy staging, never a trim).

where.loc: line 48 MuSeries greedy comment; line 70-78 muHash

entries.notes: Contrast: AFL/AniList staging hashes the whole payload (resolve.ts).

entries.statement: For recurring conditions a flag is filed only when no OPEN flag of the same kind already exists for the series key (fileFlagOnce); fileFlag always inserts. A flag records the anomaly AND the proposed data so it can be ruled on later without re-scraping; callers HOLD the change.
entries.notes: FlagKind vocabulary: parse_integrity | taxonomy_conflict | match_ambiguous | count_mismatch | large_diff. fileFlagOnce keys on (series_key, kind) only — not on source or detail, so two different count_mismatch conditions on one series collapse into one open flag.

entries.statement: Every ingest write goes through an ingest_runs row (source afl|afg|anilist|resolve, counters fetched/unchanged/changed/flagged) so provenance is queryable; lib runs under both Node (tsx, env from .env.ingest) and the Supabase Edge runtime (Deno env), using the secret/service-role key.
entries.notes: startRun's source union lacks 'mangaupdates'/'wikipedia' even though flags are filed with those source strings — the run-source vocabulary and the flag-source vocabulary have drifted.

entries.statement: Source clients: AniList is paced at 2200 ms (~27 req/min under the degraded 30/min limit, treated as permanent), batches 50 media per id_in query, retries on 429 after retry-after; scrape hosts (AFL, AFG) get a 10 s per-host floor (AFL's robots.txt Crawl-delay: 10, same courtesy to AFG) with conditional GETs (ETag/Last-Modified); MangaUpdates is paced ~1.5 s per its AUP (cache aggressively, credit MU in the footer); Wikipedia uses the action API with a contact UA. Everything lands raw in staging; promotion is the resolver's decision.
entries.notes: Contact email in UA strings is seanreedux@gmail.com (three copies: http.ts, match.ts, mangaupdates.ts, wikipedia.ts).

entries.statement: 1000-row-cap-exposed reads in lib (unpaged .select on tables that can exceed Supabase's default 1000-row page): anchors.ts#syncAnchors typeRows = episodes.select('number, type').eq('series_id') — per-series, but one-piece (~1100+) and detective-conan (1000+) exceed 1000 episode rows, so episodes past the cap look ROW-LESS to the A1 allow-list filter and pass as untyped (detective-conan has overrides at 1000/1001). Correctly paged: chain.ts#ownedAnilistIds (range loop over series_components and series). Bounded/safe: applyMuFrontier sibs (per manga), applyContinua inserts (per series components), prevCont/curated anchor selects (per series, far below 1000), all maybeSingle/limit(1) reads. Inserts are chunked at 500 (episodes, chapter_anchors).
entries.notes: Whether the project's Supabase client raises the default page size was not checked (no DB/config access this pass); if it does not, this is a live A1 gap on the two longest series. Catalog-sized tables (series, series_components) are only read paged in lib.

entries.statement: Duplicated logic across lib (drift surface for T2): stitched-aggregate derivation (resolve.ts#refreshStitchedVolatile vs chain.ts#aggregate); source_type and manga_status maps (resolve.ts vs chain.ts inline, with real divergences); token-agreement title match (resolve.ts#titlesAgree, wikipedia.ts x2, match.ts normalize); SERIES_FORMATS (chain.ts export vs match.ts local); the +10 chapter-space margin and the 12-episode alignment threshold each appear as literals in three functions; the A1 allow-list (canon/mixed) is inlined three times (applyContinua, syncAnchors, applyMuFrontier).
entries.notes: Not a rule; recorded so the T2 code-home pass can collapse each to one definition (the C3 predicate in c3.ts is the model).

entries.statement: AFL alias corruption: AFL's Drupal aliases can serve show B at /shows/A after rename collisions, in two forms — episode links keep the true alias, or the primary alias was swapped and only the index title exposes it.
entries.notes: Gated.

entries.statement: AFL numbers order-only entries (specials, bonus OVAs, films, recaps, even a PS2 game) as episodes and renumbers everything after them; a drop-only translation is not durable because AFL renumbers trailing extras after drops.

where.loc: line 362-411 SOURCE_NUMBERING_SHIFTS comments; line 84, 91 COMMUNITY_COUNT_OVERRIDES notes

entries.notes: Gated per series only (map entries), never derived.

entries.statement: AFL type labels can be wrong or absent: sparse community classification (Kinnikuman 4 of 137), tables that stop mid-series (sket-dance at 54), 'Manga Canon' credited to a spin-off manga (Boruto 282-293 / Sasuke Retsuden), manga-canon on studio endings (x 21-24), filler on episodes with page-level adaptation (hunter-x-hunter 7), anime-canon on an explicit chapter mapping (one-piece 737); a >20% type churn in one pull is a parser break.
entries.notes: Only the churn and sparse cases are gated; the rest are per-series overrides. Belongs in the research-agent definition.

entries.statement: AFL wiki-edit artifacts duplicate an episode row (same number twice).
entries.notes: Gated.

entries.statement: AFG page-shape traps: divider rows whose text propagates as an arc label; placeholder title cells '(01).'; a '* Filler' marker appended inside the title cell; a finale row typo'd to a phantom number ('155.' on a 145-row chart); summary/colspan rows that digit-concatenate; thousands-separator commas in chapter cells; episodes repeated in recap boxes.
entries.notes: The phantom-row case is gated by a per-series cap, not the parser.

entries.statement: AFG chart-value traps: stray/junk chapter values (Naruto ep 141 → ch 21), flash-forward grafts (HxH ep 83 → ch 288), stray low values beside the mainline (Oshi ep 4 '10' beside 17-19), boundary chapters double-listed across rows (Fairy Tail 277 / One Piece 510), franchise-continuous chapter numbering (Boruto 702-710 in Naruto space), and a chapter column that is a reading-position conversion plateauing across filler rows (one-piece 214/216 both 313).
bundle_parts: double-listed boundaries → equal legal, below = noise
plateau on noncanon rows → A1 filter
entries.notes: All gated.

entries.statement: AFG numbers episodes MAL-style (excluding community-numbered mid-run inserts) — so a continua 'ended at episode N' can be N+inserts in our space; and AFG's continua template can name a DIFFERENT series (SHY/Kamonohashi Ron, Cuckoos/Dandadan); and a continua episode can sit one short of the page's own chart rows (you-and-i-are-polar-opposites).
entries.notes: Conversion + identity guard are gated; the chart-vs-continua disagreement is suppressed per series only (gate candidate).

entries.statement: AniList relation traps: the ADAPTATION edge is directionless (an anime-original's linked manga adapts the anime — Evangelion/Madoka); PREQUEL edges can be chronological side stories (MONSTERS ONA as One Piece's prequel); old entries omit `source`; an announced season has 0 aired (Tokyo Revengers 51-50); Second Season counts can include recaps (monogatari).
entries.notes: All gated except recap-inflated counts (per-series cap).

entries.statement: MangaUpdates traps: latest_chapter is release-record-derived — garbage for old completed manga (Dragon Ball 149 of 519) and sometimes counts VOLUMES (Kakegurui 9); the anime field is multi-segment prose whose EP number can belong to another clause (Naruto/Boruto) and describes the whole franchise (Slime, 4KOTA, ace-ii, yowamushi) or the announced final coverage while still airing (TYBW ch 705); a pin can be count-space vs number-space (Tokyo Ghoul 144/143); status strings are multi-line; payloads carry rating/rank churn.
bundle_parts: latest_chapter unit/edition drift → same-edition band + chapter floor
multi-segment anime prose → parseCoverageAll + sibling ceiling + chapter-space
count vs number space → Tokyo Ghoul conversion
entries.notes: All gated.

entries.statement: Wikipedia traps: a mis-parsed volume start silently corrupts every downstream boundary (Sailor Moon v3 'chs 10-3'); full-text search ranking returns the wrong series (Ranma ½ for My Dress-Up Darling); episode lists live on transcluded season pages (Dr. Stone); chapter lists come in three dialects ({{Numbered list|start}}, <li value>, bare range with a series label like 'Mission: 1–5'); smart-quote entities in AFG headings.
entries.notes: All gated.

entries.statement: Sources can genuinely disagree about ONE series' numbering (mashle's recap is integer ep 7 on AFL but '6.5'/excluded on AFG, fandom, Wikipedia, AniList) — a blanket shift corrupts the already-aligned source.
entries.notes: Gated via the `spaces` field.

entries.statement: Pipeline traps (superseded designs recorded in comments): a bare DB update on a derived row is clobbered by the next refresh (hence maps that re-apply); the old 'non-MU anchor within 12 eps of run end' freshness skip and the chapter no-progress skip deleted real run-end pins (AoT ep 89, Kuroko 75, Naruto 220); the old arc-pattern anchor guard nuked whole stretches when a divider propagated as arc (Naruto 6-27); same-episode precedence cannot stop a wrong source value landing on a different episode (Claymore/Kimi); the hourly cron erodes curated continue fields on derived rows unless carried over (C2); an import that takes AFG titles but never maps its filler flag defaults every row canon (eyeshield-21); deleting to the source-space max eats rows the translation does not refill (Ryuusui); a drop-only shift lets a renumbered extra re-enter (yu-yu-hakusho 113).
entries.notes: Each has a live replacement rule (listed in parts 1-3); belongs in the apply-batch traps section.

entries.statement: AniFiller (github.com/AniraTeam/AniFiller) is unlicensed: only its AFL-slug → AniList/MAL id mapping (a fact) is used, never its episode data — our AFL scrape is the data source.
entries.notes: Enforced by construction (only mappings.anilist_id/mal_id are read).

entries.statement: MangaUpdates AUP compliance: cache aggressively, credit MangaUpdates in the footer alongside AFL/AFG, keep reasonable request spacing (~1.5 s).
entries.notes: Pacing enforced; the footer credit is a client-home obligation.
